name: MO-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+27 partisan lean makes it deeply Republican
Incumbent Jason Smith has a massive financial edge ($5.0M cash vs. under $2K for the Democrat)
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 96% to win

model.rationale: Smith holds a heavily Republican seat with a dominant fundraising advantage and near-certain market pricing, while Democrat Chris Reichard has raised only a few thousand dollars. The fundamentals and money both point to an easy incumbent win.
model.watch: A surprise would require a dramatic late shift in the national environment far beyond anything currently indicated, since no local polling exists to move the picture.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Smith is seeking another term in a southeastern Missouri district that leans Republican by roughly 27 points. He has raised more than $5.2 million and holds about $5 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Chris Reichard has raised under $6,000 and has minimal cash available. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Smith about a 96 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong partisan lean, Smith's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial advantage makes this one of the safest Republican House seats on the map this cycle.
